newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes firmer after volatile late trade.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes firmer after volatile late trade.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended firmer on Friday, having recovered from a burst of long liquidation shortly before the close.
April Brent closed 10 cents up at $19.80 a barrel, off a session high of $20.07 a barrel.

In nervous trade, dealers took Brent's failure to remain above the key $20.00 a barrel level as a signal to liquidate positions and the market slumped to session lows of $19.55 a barrel in the last hour of trade.
But strength of NYMEX heating oil, which remained firmly in the black despite shedding some early gains, gave a late shot in the arm to the whole oil complex, traders said.
"It's a battle between the shorts and the longs and the longs came out on top," said one broker.
Brent pushed back up to $20.00 in a rapid short-covering rally before easing back to the close having failed to breach the critical resistance level.
Despite weak long-term fundamentals, an expected drop in temperatures in the U.S. Northeast -- the world's key heating oil consuming region -- was serving as a short-term prop to the market.
Private forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said temperatures in the region would average five degrees Fahrenheit below normal on Friday and remain below seasonal norms throughout the weekend.
March gas oil ended $4.25 up at $169 a tonne, while the April Brent/gas oil spread closed at $2.87 a barrel, which dealers said was untenable in the longer term.
"I'm surprised gas oil closed as strong as it did, the crack is too wide to feel comfortable," said one dealer.
"If the strength was coming from gasoline rather than heat we'd be a bit more bullish," said one trader.
The longer-term outlook was more bearish, analysts said.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) said one Friday that OPEC output in February was unchanged from January at 26.98 million barrels per day.

It also said that oil inventories in the world's leading industrial nations recovered in January and ended the month higher than the year before in the first time in January to end the month higher than a year before for the first time in 18 months.

"Most background fundamentals remain essentially unchanged and on the weak side," London brokers GNI said in a daily report. "OPEC production is bearish and high at just under the psychological 27 million barrels per day, and will exceed it before long."
